chapter: Benny Carter, saxophones and Coleman Hawkins's last years
title: Meeting Hawkins at a Harlem supermarket
summary: Caldwell last saw Hawk in uptown Harlem shopping for his family; Hilton Jefferson lived in the same building.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: Oh, definitely. You know, there was so many -- the last time I saw him, he was living up there with his family on 154th Street -- 151st Street, right around the Masonic Temple. So I'm up there-- I had a group up there -- 158th Street, playing for dances, club dates, and there was a big supermarket, and Hawk drive up there with his Chrysler station wagon. Hey, Hap. I said, what do you say, King? And we started to talking. He was going in the supermarket to buy food for his family, and Milton Jackson lived in the same building, where Hawk lived.
-- not the place he had in Central Park West.

No, because he had two girls and one boy. And so we started talking a little while, and he had his Chrysler station wagon. So I said, well, when you going to leave -- when you leaving town. He said, you know, Hap, I'll be downtown. Said, why don't you come on by. So -- by all means. And we started to talking, chatting, and I walked with him, bought food for the family, and next time -- I didn't see him in about a year. And talked to Hitler (unintelligible) Jefferson, said, "didn't never hear about Hawk?" I says, no, I haven't seen Hawk since over a year ago, met him going into the supermarket.

He says, well, he living downtown, left the family, and didn't treat the family too good, from what Jeff was telling me. But Jeff was there because he was living in the saem building with his family. And they said that hetreat the family so bad, that his wife -- the tenants in the building didn't like it, and they would always look after the kids.
Now, he got a son too, but none of them played music.
